agntux-apple-notes.tagline: Capture notes from Apple Notes with one-click create and edit.
agntux-apple-notes.description:
Apple Notes syncs into AgntUX so you can see action items and reminders
in one place. Create new notes, update existing ones, and check off
items from your phone's native note app — all from AgntUX.

supported_prompts.purpose: Type /agntux-apple-notes to check for new or updated notes. Or ask a question about your notes.

ui_components.name: create-note
ui_components.title: Create Note
ui_components.purpose: Compose and save a new note to Apple Notes.

ui_components.name: update-note
ui_components.title: Update Note
ui_components.purpose: Edit an existing note, add content, or check off checklist items.

entity_subtypes.description: An Apple Note with title, content, folder, and timestamps.

action_classes.description: Create a new note in Apple Notes.
Update an existing note or check off checklist items.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Modification-time watermark; notes are de-duplicated by stable source ID and polled for updated content.

agntux-asana.tagline: See your Asana tasks that need action, right in AgntUX.
agntux-asana.description: Brings your Asana tasks and projects into AgntUX so you can see what needs your attention in one place. Check for new tasks anytime, or ask AgntUX about your work in Asana — it'll look it up and help you stay on top of deadlines, assigned work, and project updates.

ui_components.name: comment
ui_components.title: Comment on task
ui_components.purpose: Add a comment to an Asana task directly from AgntUX.

ui_components.name: complete
ui_components.title: Mark complete or update due date
ui_components.purpose: Mark a task complete or change its due date without leaving AgntUX.

ui_components.name: assign
ui_components.title: Reassign task
ui_components.purpose: Reassign a task to a team member directly in AgntUX.

ui_components.name: create
ui_components.title: Create follow-up task
ui_components.purpose: Create a new task in Asana from AgntUX without switching apps.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new Asana tasks and updates. Ask questions about your work — AgntUX searches and summarizes.

entity_subtypes.description: An Asana task with title, assignee, due date, and status.
An Asana project with name, owner, and member list.
An Asana portfolio grouping related projects.
Team members and task assignees in your Asana workspace.

action_classes.description: Task with an approaching or past due date.
Task assigned to you or mentions you in a comment.
Task status change, project update, or comment activity.
Completed task or project milestone reached.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Timestamp of newest modified task seen this run; advances for each sync.

agntux-build.tagline: Build a new AgntUX plugin for a tool AgntUX doesn't support yet.
agntux-build.description:
Step-by-step help to add a tool AgntUX doesn't support yet. You'll pick
the tool, design a simple action button, preview it, and test it against
your real data. Built for everyone, not just engineers — plain language,
a clean standard look, and a little encouragement at each step. Expect to
test it a few times until it feels right; that's completely normal.

supported_prompts.purpose: Walks you through building a plugin for a tool AgntUX doesn't support yet. Can also fix an existing plugin if you've run into something specific.

agntux-calendly.tagline: Track Calendly bookings and send one-click cancellations and confirmations.
agntux-calendly.description: Watches your Calendly bookings and surfaces what needs your attention—new inbound leads, upcoming meetings that might need rescheduling, and attendees marked as no-shows. Cancel meetings or send follow-ups right from AgntUX.
data_ingested: Scheduled meetings with attendee info and status
Inbound booking requests and lead submissions

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new Calendly bookings and leads, or ask questions about your scheduled meetings and attendees.

ui_components.name: agntux-calendly-cancel
ui_components.title: Cancel Calendly meeting
ui_components.purpose: Review and confirm cancellation of a scheduled Calendly meeting, with an editable reason sent to the Calendly Connector.

ui_components.name: agntux-calendly-no-show
ui_components.title: Mark Calendly invitees as no-show
ui_components.purpose: Select one or more attendees from a past meeting and mark them as no-shows via the Calendly Connector.

ui_components.name: agntux-calendly-scheduling-link
ui_components.title: Create single-use Calendly booking link
ui_components.purpose: Choose an event type and generate a single-use Calendly booking link that expires after one booking.

entity_subtypes.description: A booked meeting on your calendar with attendee details and confirmation status.
A bookable meeting template defining duration, availability, and meeting details.
Meeting attendees and invitees, with contact info and attendance status.

action_classes.description: New booking requests or inbound leads requiring your confirmation or follow-up.
Upcoming meetings approaching their scheduled time, or attendees unable to confirm.
Meeting cancellations, no-show follow-ups, and rescheduling requests.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Time window over scheduled events, advancing by updated_at timestamp to capture new bookings, attendee changes, and lead submissions.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{scheduled_event_uuid}` for meetings, `{invitee_uuid}` for attendees, `{event_type_uuid}` for templates.

agntux-core.tagline: Your AgntUX home base — onboarding and your daily action-items list.
agntux-core.description:
AgntUX Core is the first thing you install — every other AgntUX plugin
builds on it.

Start with `/agntux onboard` to get set up. After that, `/agntux triage`
is your everyday command: it shows your action items, sorted by what
matters most, with one-click buttons to snooze, dismiss, or mark
something done.

As your other plugins bring in updates from Slack, Gmail, and your
calendar, Core keeps everything organized and ready whenever you ask.

supported_prompts.purpose: **`/agntux onboard`** — DO THIS FIRST - and then again any time you install a new plugin. This runs your onboarding flow and gets everything set up.
**`/agntux triage`** — This is your go-to command after you're onboarded. Use this to see your action items list. You'll be using this command all day every day.
**`/agntux`** — Ask anything about your information, edit your profile, teach a plugin a rule, or sync a source.

ui_components.name: triage
ui_components.title: Action item triage
ui_components.purpose: Your open action items in priority order, each with snooze, dismiss, and done buttons — plus quick buttons that take you straight into the right plugin to act.

agntux-docusign.tagline: Track DocuSign envelopes and stay on top of what needs your signature.
agntux-docusign.description: Brings DocuSign e-signature workflows into your AgntUX knowledge store. See envelopes out for signature, track who still needs to sign, surface action items for pending signers, and flag agreements approaching renewal or expiration. One-click actions let you send reminder nudges or open signing ceremonies directly in DocuSign.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new DocuSign envelopes and agreements. Or ask a question about your DocuSign — it just looks things up.

data_ingested: Envelopes with status (created, sent, delivered, signed, completed, declined, voided)
Signers and their signing status for each envelope

ui_components.name: agntux-docusign-reminder
ui_components.title: Send Reminder
ui_components.purpose: Notify pending signers that an envelope is awaiting their signature.

ui_components.name: agntux-docusign-void
ui_components.title: Void Envelope
ui_components.purpose: Cancel an envelope and notify all recipients with a void reason.

ui_components.name: agntux-docusign-sign
ui_components.title: Review and Sign
ui_components.purpose: Open a signing ceremony to review and sign an envelope waiting for your signature.

entity_subtypes.description: A signature request or transaction with a lifecycle: created, sent, delivered, signed, completed, declined, or voided.
An executed or managed contract with parties, status, and renewal/expiration provisions.

action_classes.description: A signer must take action (sign/complete), or reminders are needed for pending signers.
Envelope or agreement status change (voided, declined, completed) or renewal/expiration milestone.
Miscellaneous DocuSign signals.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: High-watermark on envelope last-modified time. Agreements paginate via cursor with created_at/modified_at watermarks.

agntux-dropbox.tagline: Bring your Dropbox files into AgntUX, and act on them instantly.
agntux-dropbox.description:
Watches your Dropbox for files and folders that need your attention. Share
links, organize files, create folders, and request uploads—all from triage,
without leaving AgntUX. Syncs every 4 hours during work hours.
data_ingested: Files and their metadata (names, sizes, timestamps, sharing status)

supported_prompts.purpose: Check Dropbox for updates, or ask a question about your files. The plugin searches and looks them up for you.

ui_components.name: share-file
ui_components.title: Share a file
ui_components.purpose: Create a shareable link to a file and copy it to send. Control who can access and whether they can download.

ui_components.name: organize-file
ui_components.title: Move or copy a file
ui_components.purpose: Move a file to a different folder or create a copy. Choose the destination folder and confirm.

ui_components.name: new-folder
ui_components.title: Create a folder
ui_components.purpose: Create a new folder in your Dropbox. Give it a name and choose where to put it.

ui_components.name: file-request
ui_components.title: Request a file
ui_components.purpose: Set up a file request link to ask people to upload files. They don't need a Dropbox account to send.

entity_subtypes.description: A document or file stored in Dropbox with content and metadata.
A directory or container in Dropbox holding files and subfolders.
A publicly shareable link to a file or folder with permissions.
A request link where people can upload files to a folder.

action_classes.description: A file or folder that needs your attention to share, organize, or action.
New or updated files and folders added to your Dropbox.
Files or folders that present a chance to share or collaborate.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Four-part cursor: folder_cursor (server delta), files (file_id to rev map), shared_links_cursor, file_requests_seen; all advance transactionally. Bootstrap backfill when cursor is null.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{file_id}` — Dropbox's stable unique ID per file/folder; rev indicates changes.

agntux-gmail.tagline: See the emails that need a reply, and draft responses safely.
agntux-gmail.description:
Brings your Gmail into AgntUX. It spots the emails that need a reply —
messages to you, threads you're waiting on, replies you owe — and drafts a
response for you. It only ever saves to your Gmail Drafts; you review and
hit Send in Gmail.
data_ingested: Inbox threads where you are in to: or cc:
Threads where you have sent a message and someone has replied since
Your sent items awaiting reply for ≥3 days
Threads carrying the IMPORTANT Gmail label
Subject lines and short previews from related conversations, used to write better replies

supported_prompts.purpose: Type `/agntux-gmail` to check for new email now. Or ask a question about your inbox — that just looks things up, it doesn't change anything.

ui_components.name: compose
ui_components.title: Gmail reply composer
ui_components.purpose: Write a reply right here — edit the recipients, subject, and body, with context from your past emails. Save puts it in your Gmail Drafts and opens it for you to review and send.

entity_subtypes.description: Email correspondents — senders, recipients, cc'd colleagues. Email address is the canonical cross-source alias used to merge with people surfaced by Slack and other sources.
Organisations resolved from sender email domains and signature blocks. Vendors, customers, partners surfaced via correspondence.
Workstreams or codenames mentioned in email subjects and bodies (often resolved via user.md → # Glossary).
Recurring themes or initiatives surfaced across multiple email threads.

action_classes.description: An email carrying an explicit due date or time-bound ask.
An email addressed to the user (to: or cc:) or a thread where someone has replied since the user's last message and a reply is expected.
An informational signal extracted from an email thread (decision summary, status update, important announcement).
Outage, incident, security, or escalation signals that warrant urgent attention.
Sales, partnership, or market signal in an email thread.
Escape hatch for items that don't fit the above; requires reason_detail.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Single JSON map (one line). Two key shapes: `inbox` for the discovery low-water-mark (Gmail epoch-seconds); `<thread_id>` for per-thread cursors (newest message internalDate processed).
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<thread_id>` for thread-rooted artefacts; `<thread_id>#<message_id>` for per-message artefacts when needed.

agntux-google-calendar.tagline: A daily look at your week ahead, with everything you need to prepare.
agntux-google-calendar.description:
Brings your Google Calendar into AgntUX. Each morning it reads the week
ahead and, for every meeting, pulls together what you need to prepare —
related Slack threads, emails, and past notes — right where you'll see it.
When you want to act, two buttons let you find a time and schedule a
meeting, or accept, tentatively accept, or decline an invite.
data_ingested: Upcoming events on all your calendars over the next 7 days
Each event's attendees, location, description, video link, and organizer

supported_prompts.purpose: Type `/agntux-google-calendar` to check your upcoming calendar now. Or ask a question about your schedule — it just looks things up.

ui_components.name: schedule
ui_components.title: Find a time and schedule the meeting
ui_components.purpose: Pick who to invite and a rough window; AgntUX shows the open slots. Choose one and Send creates the meeting with your prep notes attached.

ui_components.name: respond
ui_components.title: Accept, tentatively accept, or decline the invite
ui_components.purpose: See the invite with any conflicts and your prep notes. Accept, tentatively accept, or decline — with an optional note to the organizer.

entity_subtypes.description: People invited to your events, matched up by email address.
Resolved from email domains in attendee lists.
Project names found in event titles and descriptions.
Recurring meeting themes — standups, weekly syncs, customer reviews.

action_classes.description: An event with hard prep work due before start; e.g. review deck, submit Q3 numbers.
An invite the user has not yet responded to.
An upcoming meeting the user is attending needs prep context surfaced before start.
Conflict, double-booking, or critical-meeting overlap.
A recurring meeting whose summary or outcome should be captured post-event.
Escape hatch for calendar events not fitting the above classes.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: JSON map with `look_ahead_window_end` (RFC3339) and per-event `<calendar_id>#<event_id>` → `updated` timestamp pairs. Past events evict on each sync pass.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<calendar_id>#<event_id>` for events; add `#<occurrence_start>` for recurring event instances.

agntux-google-drive.tagline: Bring your Google Drive files into your AgntUX knowledge store.
agntux-google-drive.description: Keep your most important Google Drive documents and spreadsheets in sync with AgntUX. Search files by title, content, or date; read document content; and get a heads-up when a doc changes or when someone mentions you in a comment — each with a link straight to the file. Perfect for staying on top of shared projects and recent updates.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new files and updates. Ask questions about your Drive — it searches and reads for you.

data_ingested: Change alerts when a tracked doc is updated

entity_subtypes.description: A Google Doc text document.
A Google Sheet spreadsheet.
A Google Slides presentation.
A PDF file stored in Google Drive.
A folder in Google Drive.
Other file types (images, videos, archives, etc.).

action_classes.description: A tracked document was updated with new content.
You were mentioned in a document comment or assignment.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Time-based cursor tracking the most recent modifiedTime of files seen.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: Google Drive file ID (stable identifier, e.g. 1cguDW1J6QA…)

agntux-hubspot.tagline: Manage HubSpot deals, tasks, and tickets without leaving AgntUX.
agntux-hubspot.description: Watches your HubSpot account for deals approaching close dates, tasks coming due, and tickets needing replies. See recent customer activity and who's assigned to what, then move deals between stages, complete or reschedule tasks, log notes on records, and reassign work — all without switching to HubSpot.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new deals, tasks, and tickets. Or ask about your HubSpot records to search and find information.

ui_components.name: move-deal-stage
ui_components.title: Move deal to a new stage
ui_components.purpose: Transition a deal between sales pipeline stages.

ui_components.name: update-task
ui_components.title: Complete or reschedule task
ui_components.purpose: Mark a task complete or set a new due date.

ui_components.name: log-activity
ui_components.title: Log note or activity
ui_components.purpose: Add a note, call, email, or meeting to a customer record.

ui_components.name: reassign-record
ui_components.title: Reassign to another owner
ui_components.purpose: Transfer a deal, ticket, or contact to a team member.

entity_subtypes.description: A sales opportunity or deal in your HubSpot pipeline.
A person in your HubSpot database.
An organization in your HubSpot database.
A task or reminder assigned in HubSpot.
A customer support ticket in HubSpot.
A note, call, email, or meeting logged on a record.

action_classes.description: A deal close date or task due date approaching soon.
A ticket or assignment waiting for your action.
A status change or update on a deal, contact, or ticket.
A stale or stuck deal, or an overdue task.
A newly assigned deal, contact, or task to follow up on.
A HubSpot event or notification that doesn't fit another class.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Per-entity-type cursor map tracking the most recent hs_lastmodifieddate; advances to mark processed objects.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{object_type}#{hs_object_id}` — HubSpot object IDs are unique per object type.

agntux-imessage.tagline: See the iMessages that need a reply, sorted by priority.
agntux-imessage.description: Watches your iMessages for conversations that need you—from known contacts with urgent questions to marketing messages. Brings them into AgntUX sorted by priority (replies needed, personal messages, promotional) so you focus on what matters most. Lets you draft and review replies before sending.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new messages, or ask a question about your iMessages—it looks them up.

ui_components.name: reply
ui_components.title: Reply to message
ui_components.purpose: Send a reply to the sender. The AI drafts a response you review and confirm before sending.

entity_subtypes.description: Individuals you message with. Identified by phone number or email.

action_classes.description: An iMessage conversation awaiting a reply from you.
A message with information to note or remember.
Messages that don't fit standard categories.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Per-contact last-seen timestamp; advances to the newest message in each conversation seen this run.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{phone_or_email}#{message_id}` — message_id is the rowid in the iMessage database.

agntux-jira.tagline: See your Jira issues and act on them without leaving your workflow.
agntux-jira.description: Brings your Jira issues into AgntUX so the work that needs you shows up in one place. See assignments, replies on watched issues, and work that's stalling — then comment, transition, assign, edit, or log time directly from AgntUX.

supported_prompts.purpose: Type `/agntux-jira` to check for new Jira issues and updates now. Or ask a question about your Jira — it just looks things up.

ui_components.name: comment-issue
ui_components.title: Comment on issue
ui_components.purpose: Add a comment to a Jira issue.

ui_components.name: transition-issue
ui_components.title: Transition issue
ui_components.purpose: Change an issue's status (e.g., In Progress to In Review).

ui_components.name: assign-issue
ui_components.title: Assign issue
ui_components.purpose: Assign an issue to a person or team.

ui_components.name: edit-issue-fields
ui_components.title: Edit issue details
ui_components.purpose: Update priority, labels, summary, or other issue fields.

ui_components.name: log-work-time
ui_components.title: Log time
ui_components.purpose: Record work hours spent on an issue.

entity_subtypes.description: A Jira issue or task that appears in a project.
A comment left on a Jira issue.
A workflow state change available for an issue.
A time entry logged against an issue.

action_classes.description: An issue is waiting for a reply or action from the user.
An issue requires a decision or state change as an SLA approaches.
A status update or new information on a watched issue.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Per-project cursor map keyed by projectKey; value is the most-recent issue updated timestamp in ISO8601 format.

agntux-mercury.tagline: Track spending, balances, and approvals from Mercury in AgntUX.
agntux-mercury.description: Brings your Mercury account balances, transactions, cards, and pending approvals into AgntUX so they surface alongside your other work. See cash flow, credit usage, spending by category, and what's waiting for you to sign off on — all in one place.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check Mercury for new transactions and approvals, or ask about balances and cards.

data_ingested: Transactions with counterparty, amount, and category
Virtual and physical card status and spend
Mercury credit (IO) balance and available limit

entity_subtypes.description: A Mercury checking, savings, or treasury account with current balance and account type.
A money movement in or out of a Mercury account with counterparty, amount, posted/pending status, and category.
A virtual or physical Mercury debit card with status, cardholder, spend limit, and last four digits.
Mercury IO credit line with current balance and available credit limit.
A pending send money request waiting for authorization from a team member.
An incoming or outgoing invoice tied to a customer or recipient with amount and status.
A saved payment recipient for future send money transactions.
A customer or client connected to incoming or outgoing invoices.
A user in the Mercury organization who can approve send money requests and sign documents.
The Mercury workspace/organization with basic settings and member count.

action_classes.description: Invoice due dates approaching or past due.
Send money request awaiting your approval or signature.
New account, card, balance, or recipient information from Mercury.
Unusual transaction pattern, low balance alert, or card status change.
Available credit limit on Mercury IO.
Emerging Mercury signal not yet categorized.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Incremental cursor over transaction timestamps. Each account's cursor advances to the most recent createdAt. Accounts, cards, and approvals refresh each run; statements and invoices pull periodically.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{resource_type}#{uuid}` — each resource has a UUID unique within its type.

agntux-notion.tagline: Notion tasks and updates in AgntUX, with direct replies and edits.
agntux-notion.description:
Brings your Notion workspace into AgntUX so tasks, projects, and
pages that need you show up in one place. Reply to comments, update
page properties, and create new pages without leaving AgntUX. Check
for new activity every 4 hours or ask a question about your Notion
anytime.

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new activity in Notion, or ask a question about your workspace.

ui_components.name: reply-to-comment
ui_components.title: Reply to comment
ui_components.purpose: Write a reply to a comment on a Notion page.

ui_components.name: update-page
ui_components.title: Update page
ui_components.purpose: Edit properties and fields on a Notion page.

ui_components.name: create-page
ui_components.title: Create page
ui_components.purpose: Create a new page in your Notion workspace.

entity_subtypes.description: A page in your Notion workspace — docs, wiki pages, or standalone notes.
A row in a Notion database — tasks, projects, or custom items you track.
A comment or mention thread on a page or database item.
A Notion user or person mentioned in comments and assignments.

action_classes.description: A comment on a page or item that mentions you or waits for your reply.
A page or database item that was created or updated with new information.
A task or project with a due date in Notion.
A page or item marked as important or worth reviewing.
Any other actionable item from Notion that doesn't fit a standard class.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Tracks the last-edited timestamp of pages and database items. Comments are polled per page each run; the plugin checks for new comment activity alongside page updates.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{block-id}` — Notion's 32-character hex UUID (dashed format) uniquely identifies each page, database item, and comment.

agntux-posthog.tagline: Bring PostHog analytics signals into AgntUX for faster decision-making.
agntux-posthog.description:
Watch your PostHog errors, alerts, experiments, and flagged reports right in AgntUX.
Triage error issues, acknowledge alerts, decide on experiments, and resolve reports—
all with one-click actions that sync back to PostHog. See the product signals that
need a human decision in one central place.
data_ingested: Error tracking issues (status, error type, affected users)
Alert firings (alert rule, severity, trigger time)
Experiment state and results (test name, variant performance)
Comment mentions and threads (comment author, content)
Inbox flagged reports (flag reason, report type)

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new PostHog signals now. Or ask about your analytics data—it just looks things up.

ui_components.name: resolve
ui_components.title: Resolve Error Issue
ui_components.purpose: Resolve or reassign a PostHog error issue.

ui_components.name: reply
ui_components.title: Reply to Comment
ui_components.purpose: Reply to a PostHog comment thread.

ui_components.name: experiment
ui_components.title: Ship Experiment Variant
ui_components.purpose: Ship the winning variant of a PostHog experiment.

ui_components.name: report
ui_components.title: Mark Report Handled
ui_components.purpose: Mark a flagged PostHog inbox report as handled.

entity_subtypes.description: A tracked error in your product with stack trace, affected users, and resolution status.
A fired alert rule monitoring your product metrics or events.
An A/B test or multivariate experiment measuring feature impact.
A discussion thread on an error issue or insight with mentions and replies.
A flagged or anomaly-detected item in your PostHog inbox awaiting triage.

action_classes.description: Acknowledge or triage an alert, error issue, or flagged report that requires human attention.
Resolve or close an error issue by a deadline or once mitigated.
Document experiment results, insights, or dashboard findings.
Decide on an experiment variant or take action based on flagged data.
Escalate or flag a critical error, anomaly, or experiment regression.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Per-resource timestamp map: errors by last_seen, alerts by fired_at, experiments by updated_at, comments by created_at, inbox reports by created_at. Cursor advances independently per resource.

agntux-sentry.tagline: See the Sentry issues that need you, right in AgntUX.
agntux-sentry.description: Brings your Sentry issues into AgntUX so the errors and problems that need you show up in one place. See new, unresolved, and escalating issues — then resolve, ignore/archive, or assign them without leaving AgntUX.

supported_prompts.purpose: Type /agntux-sentry to check for new issues now. Or ask a question about your Sentry — it just looks things up.

ui_components.name: resolve-issue
ui_components.title: Resolve issue
ui_components.purpose: Mark a Sentry issue as resolved.

ui_components.name: ignore-issue
ui_components.title: Ignore issue
ui_components.purpose: Archive or ignore a Sentry issue.

ui_components.name: assign-issue
ui_components.title: Assign issue
ui_components.purpose: Assign a Sentry issue to a team member or team.

entity_subtypes.description: A Sentry issue — a grouped error or problem affecting your apps.

action_classes.description: A new or escalating Sentry issue that needs triage or action.
An informational signal from a Sentry issue (status change, comment added).

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Per-project incremental cursor; advances to the newest issue last-seen timestamp. Issues re-surface if they escalate after being archived.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{short_id}` — Sentry's short issue id, project-prefixed and globally unique (e.g. `agntux-app-1`).

agntux-slack.tagline: See the Slack messages that need a reply, and draft responses safely.
agntux-slack.description:
Brings your Slack into AgntUX. It spots the messages that need a reply —
your DMs, mentions, and threads — and drafts a response for you to review.
Nothing posts until you press Send.
data_ingested: DMs (1:1) and group DMs in your workspace
@mentions of you in any channel you have access to
Threads where you are OP or have replied
Channel messages in any channel you have authored in recently
Pinned messages and canvases referenced from monitored channels

supported_prompts.purpose: Type `/agntux-slack` to check for new messages now. Or ask a question about your Slack — that just looks things up, it doesn't change anything.

ui_components.name: compose
ui_components.title: Slack reply composer
ui_components.purpose: Write a reply right here with the thread for context. Send it now, schedule it for later, or save it as a draft.

ui_components.name: canvas
ui_components.title: Slack canvas summariser
ui_components.purpose: Turn a thread into a Slack canvas summary. Edit the title, recap, decisions, open questions, and who was involved, then post it to the thread.

entity_subtypes.description: Slack users — DM partners, channel co-authors, mentioned colleagues. Email from profile is the cross-source alias.
Organizations referenced in Slack — vendors, customers, partners surfaced via shared links or named in messages.
Workstreams or codenames mentioned in channels and threads (often resolved via user.md → # Glossary).
Recurring themes, products, or initiatives surfaced across multiple Slack threads.

action_classes.description: A Slack message carrying an explicit due date or time-bound ask.
A DM, @mention, vote/poll, or thread reply that expects a response from the user.
An informational signal extracted from a Slack thread (decision, status update, pinned message).
Outage/incident/security signal in a monitored ops or security channel; @here / @channel pings to high-stakes channels.
Competitor or market signal in a sales/marketing channel; prospect activity or partnership cues.
Escape hatch for items that don't fit the above; requires reason_detail.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Single JSON map (one line) under `cursor`. Two key shapes: `<channel_id>` for channel cursors (newest parent ts), `<channel_id>#<thread_ts>` for thread cursors (newest reply ts).
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `<channel_id>#<thread_ts>` for thread-rooted artefacts; `<channel_id>#<ts>` for non-threaded messages.

agntux-stripe.tagline: See Stripe updates in AgntUX with actions to refund, respond, and manage.
agntux-stripe.description:
Tracks changes in your Stripe account so you know when payments need refunds,
invoices need action, subscriptions change, or disputes arrive. One click to
refund a payment, respond to a dispute, finalize or void an invoice, or pause
and manage a subscription — no Stripe dashboard required.

supported_prompts.purpose: Type /agntux-stripe to check for new Stripe activity. Or ask about your payments, invoices, and customers — it searches your Stripe account.

ui_components.name: refund
ui_components.title: Refund payment
ui_components.purpose: Issue a full or partial refund on a Stripe charge. Select the amount and reason, then confirm.

ui_components.name: dispute
ui_components.title: Respond to dispute
ui_components.purpose: Submit evidence to respond to a Stripe chargeback dispute before the deadline.

ui_components.name: invoice-finalize
ui_components.title: Finalize invoice
ui_components.purpose: Lock and send a Stripe draft invoice to the customer.

ui_components.name: invoice-void
ui_components.title: Void invoice
ui_components.purpose: Mark a Stripe invoice as void. This action is irreversible.

ui_components.name: subscription-edit
ui_components.title: Edit subscription
ui_components.purpose: Pause collection or update the quantity on a Stripe subscription.

ui_components.name: subscription-cancel
ui_components.title: Cancel subscription
ui_components.purpose: Cancel a Stripe subscription at the end of the billing period or immediately.

entity_subtypes.description: A charge or payment processed in your Stripe account.
An invoice created in your Stripe account.
A subscription in your Stripe account.
A customer in your Stripe account.
A disputed charge in your Stripe account.
A refund processed in your Stripe account.
A coupon or discount code in your Stripe account.
A product or item sold in your Stripe account.
A pricing tier for a product in your Stripe account.
Money transferred to your bank account from Stripe.

action_classes.description: Invoice or payment deadline that needs attention.
Dispute evidence needed or customer action required.
A change in payment status, customer info, or subscription.
A failed payment, high-risk dispute, or billing issue.
A new subscription or customer to track or follow up on.
A Stripe event that doesn't fit another category.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Stripe objects have `created` timestamps; a cursor advances to track new objects each sync.
proposed_schema.source_id_format: `{resource_type}#{object_id}` — Stripe object IDs are prefixed by type (e.g. `pi_`, `ch_`, `in_`, `sub_`, `cus_`).

agntux-zoom.tagline: Your Zoom meetings, summaries, and next steps in one place.
agntux-zoom.description: Brings your Zoom into AgntUX so you never miss a meeting action item. See when you have recordings waiting, check AI-generated summaries, and save meeting outcomes directly to Zoom Docs. Opens in Zoom for quick access.
data_ingested: Meeting action items and next steps

supported_prompts.purpose: Check for new Zoom meetings and messages. Or ask about your recent meetings and action items.

ui_components.name: save-doc
ui_components.title: Save to Zoom Doc
ui_components.purpose: Saves a meeting summary and action items to a new Zoom Doc for easy reference and sharing.

entity_subtypes.description: A scheduled or completed Zoom meeting carrying topic, time, host, participants, the AI summary, next steps, and a recording link when available.
A Zoom Team Chat channel or DM thread, carrying channel/sender context and recent message text.
A Zoom Doc or Notes file used for collaborative notes and meeting outcomes.
A meeting participant or chat sender, identified by email where available.

action_classes.description: A meeting or followup with a specific date or time.
An action item, follow-up question, or decision awaiting the user's input.
A meeting summary, transcript, or recorded content to review.
A missed meeting, unreviewed recording, or unread message alert.
A notable meeting outcome or collaborative opportunity to explore.
Other Zoom signals not fitting the above categories.

proposed_schema.cursor_semantics: Dual-key timestamp window cursor — meetings_since (meetings + recordings) and chat_since (Team Chat + Docs); each stream advances independently as ISO-8601 UTC.
